sql: select * from corpus_segments where wylie like ? order by course,seq

rows.acip: YI DVAGS KYIS CHU KLUNG LA BLTAS PA NA RNAG KHRAG MTHONG BA DE YANG YI DVAGS 'GA' ZHIG LA YIN GYI, YI DVAGS THAMS CAD LA MA YIN TE, YI DVAGS LA PHYI'I SGRIB PA CAN, NANG GI SGRIB PA CAN, ZAS SKOM NYID LA YOD PA'I SGRIB PA CAN DU MA YOD PA'I PHYIR,
rows.wylie: yi dvags kyis chu klung la bltas pa na rnag khrag mthong ba de yang yi dvags 'ga' zhig la yin gyi, yi dvags thams cad la ma yin te, yi dvags la phyi'i sgrib pa can, nang gi sgrib pa can, zas skom nyid la yod pa'i sgrib pa can du ma yod pa'i phyir
rows.english: When we say that a craving spirit looks at a stream of water and sees pus and blood, by the way, we are only talking about some kinds of craving spirits, and not all of them. This is because there are many kinds of craving spirits: some with obstacles in the world around them that prevent them from relieving their craving; some with obstacles that are parts of their bodies; and some with obstacles that relate to the food or drink itself.

rows.acip: YANG KHA CIG, YI DVAGS KYIS CHU KLUNG LA BLTAS PA DE'I TSE, CHU KLUNG BSKAMS PA LA TSAD MAR SONG BA'I DE'I MIG SHES DANG , 'BRAS BU CAN GYI LJON PA LA BLTAS PA DE'I TSE, 'BRAS BU MED PA LA TSAD MAR SONG BA'I DE'I MIG SHES TSAD MA YOD PAR THAL, 'GRO BA GSUM GYIS BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA PHOR PA GANG LA BLTAS PA DE'I TSE, RNAG KHRAG DNGOS GNAS PA LA TSAD MAR SONG BA'I YI DVAGS KYI MIG SHES TSAD MA YOD PA'I PHYIR,
rows.wylie: yang kha cig, yi dvags kyis chu klung la bltas pa de'i tshe, chu klung bskams pa la tshad mar song ba'i de'i mig shes dang , 'bras bu can gyi ljon pa la bltas pa de'i tshe, 'bras bu med pa la tshad mar song ba'i de'i mig shes tshad ma yod par thal, 'gro ba gsum gyis brlan zhing gsher ba phor pa gang la bltas pa de'i tshe, rnag khrag dngos gnas pa la tshad mar song ba'i yi dvags kyi mig shes tshad ma yod pa'i phyir
rows.english: Yet again, another argument might be made: Let's take the case of one of those craving spirits that looks at a river of water, and sees it as a dry riverbed, genuinely so. Or consider one that looks at a tree loaded with fruit, but sees it as nothing but bare limbs, genuinely so. The visual consciousness of both of these beings then must be a valid perception. Why? Remember the case of the three different beings looking at a glass full of something wet and flowing; according to you, the pus and blood was actual pus and blood, and the perception of them by the craving spirit was genuine: his visual consciousness was a valid perception.
